title: Electric and Magnetic Fields
hook: How does a magnet pull a paperclip it isn't touching? Through a field — an invisible region of influence that tells other charges and magnets how to feel a force.
key_points: A field is the region around a charge or magnet that exerts force on others without contact.
Electric field lines point away from positive charges and toward negative ones.
Magnetic field lines loop from a magnet's north pole around to its south pole.
Fields carry energy, and a changing electric or magnetic field creates the other.
content_html: Reach a magnet toward a paperclip and the clip jumps before they ever touch. The thing reaching across the gap is a field — an invisible region of influence surrounding any charge or magnet. A field doesn't push anything by itself; it tells other charges and magnets how strong a force to feel and in which direction.
extra_html: We picture fields with lines. Electric field lines stream away from positive charges and into negative ones; magnetic field lines loop out of a magnet's north pole and curve back into its south. These lines aren't just bookkeeping — fields genuinely carry energy and momentum through empty space. The deepest part is the coupling: a changing electric field gives rise to a magnetic field, and a changing magnetic field gives rise to an electric one. That mutual creation is exactly what lets forces act at a distance and what makes light possible. Wikipedia describes the electromagnetic field and how its two parts intertwine.

related.title: Electric Charge & Current
related.hook: Everything electrical comes down to charge — and an electric current is simply charge on the move.

related.title: Electricity & Magnetism Are One Force
related.hook: Move a magnet near a wire and you make electricity; run current through a wire and you make a magnet. They're two faces of the same force.

flashcards.prompt: What is a field, in the context of charges and magnets?
flashcards.back_html: A region of influence around a charge or magnet that tells other charges and magnets how to feel a force — letting forces act without contact.

flashcards.prompt: Which way do electric field lines point near a positive charge?
flashcards.explanation_html: By convention, electric field lines point away from positive charges and toward negative ones, showing the direction of force on a positive test charge.

flashcards.prompt: What happens when an electric or magnetic field changes over time?

choices.text: It creates the other kind of field

flashcards.explanation_html: A changing electric field produces a magnetic field and vice versa — the coupling that underlies electromagnetism and light.
